Bible Evolution Method 3: Key Phrases

Ten separate agents each start from one random key phrase and every paste copies a string with a chance of adding or swapping or changing one whole key phrase and no deleting while a reader favors strings where neighboring phrases are also neighbors in the Bible and where single joining words fit the gaps between rebuilt stretches.

Which part of the Bible the key phrases come from

A key phrase is a short piece of about four words such as "i shall lack nothing" or "in green pastures" which a program cut from the World English Bible at punctuation marks and before linking words such as "and" and "for" and "in". The World English Bible is a modern English translation that anyone may copy freely.

String the reader likes most right now

Warning about a wording change: Charles replaces the name "yahweh" with the word "god" everywhere in this program as a personal reading choice that helps Charles follow the quotes which means the quotes here differ from the World English Bible at every place where the World English Bible prints the name.

Phrases that sit beside a true Bible neighbor show underlined in color and loose phrases show faded and joining words show in a second color. Agents may put the rebuilt stretches in any order and may place joining words in the gaps. The joining words are common linking and pointing words plus the most used naming words and action words and describing words of the chosen selection (). A stretch can jump between two places in the Bible at a phrase that appears in both places such as "i tell you" because the reader only checks one pair of neighbors at a time.

Rebuilt text over experiment time

The line shows how many phrases of an average agent sit inside a rebuilt stretch of Bible text which means a rising line shows the agents are putting more of the chopped text back together.

The best string of each separate agent

Each agent keeps a private pool of strings and never sees the strings of another agent which means each agent can rebuild different parts of the Bible.
